# Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The U.S. government took two distinct steps to end its use and exclude it from future GPS systems.

In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the government stopped using Selective Availability to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. That was an operational change: the existing feature was no longer being used.

In September 2007, the government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. This was a separate step, addressing the design of a future generation rather than switching off the feature in 2000. By excluding it from GPS III, the procurement decision made the 2000 policy durable for that generation.
